messages:
Maya Singh: quick check — API shape decision for internal control plane. debating a typed facade (proto-first, gRPC on the wire) vs a lightweight JSON proxy (HTTP/JSON passthrough). want to capture tradeoffs for telemetry, quota propagation, and rollout UX. thoughts?
Alex Chen: +1 to documenting tradeoffs. my brain: typed facade = clearer contracts + compile-time client errors. cons: more stubs, harder for ad-hoc debug, needs proto compatibility story. :thinking:
Priya Rao: typed facade helps the console team a lot — dashboards can rely on stable field names and typed metrics. we currently spend time mapping schemas in the console ingest.
Jamal Bryant: lightweight proxy wins for rapid iterations and flexibility. less churn when adding optional fields. but quota/tenant headers get lost or munged all the time in passthrough proxies. we need reliable attribute propagation for billing.
Maya Singh: exact: quota propagation is the sticking point. with typed facade we can normalize attributes server-side (tenant_id, route_claims, model_variant) before routing to infra. with proxy we rely on clients to set headers consistently which they don't.
Alex Chen: can we do a hybrid? typed facade for critical routes (billing, auth, routing) and a permissive passthrough for lower-risk endpoints? then console/telemetry can subscribe to the typed facade stream for canonical events.
Priya Rao: hybrid seems pragmatic. one implementation risk: routing policies need to be enforced uniformly. if some traffic bypasses facade we need a fallback telemetry/attribution shim at the gateway. that shim needs to attach canonical attrs for downstream.
Jamal Bryant: sketch: gateway -> auth filter -> attribute-normalizer (adds canonical attrs) -> route to target (gRPC or HTTP). attribute-normalizer could be Envoy Lua / WASM or a small service. advantage: keeps client surface simple. downside: more moving parts.
Alex Chen: proto snippet for typed facade (very small):
```proto
service ControlPlane {
  rpc ResolveRoute(RouteRequest) returns (RouteResponse);
}
message RouteRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string resource = 2;
}
```
If we commit to proto-first, we should enforce field deprecation rules and automatic descriptor publishing for clients.
Maya Singh: rollout UX: console needs canary signals at route-level (pct of requests, latency, error budget). typed facade makes it trivial to add route-level labels into traces and metrics. proxy-only path would need the attribute-normalizer to also emit identical labels.
Priya Rao: telemetry teams: we'd prefer fewer adapters. typed facade + central event emitter = single source of truth for route telemetry. can the facade emit structured events to our kafka topic?
Jamal Bryant: infra-bot: deploy check — we currently have a canary pipeline for control plane services. facade would be an additional deployable. healthcheck: /healthz and readiness gating on schema registry availability.
infra-bot: :white_check_mark: deployment pipeline found: control-plane/canary exists. add new job: control-plane/facade-canary if choosing typed facade.
Alex Chen: performance: additional RPC hop for facade. need benchmarks. if typed facade collocates with gateway (same process) that reduces network cost but increases coupling.
Maya Singh: action items: 1) Priya to list top 8 routes console depends on and whether typed fields are required; 2) Jamal to prototype attribute-normalizer as Envoy WASM and measure latency; 3) Alex to run microbench of co-located facade vs sidecar proxy. i'll consolidate decisions in an RFC draft.
Priya Rao: I'll add the console telemetry keys we need and mark which are blocking for rollout.
Jamal Bryant: I'll throw together a tiny envoy-wasm that injects x-canonical-tenant and emits a tiny histogram for added latency.
Alex Chen: ping me once you have latencies. also let's include a fallback plan: if facade rollout breaks, route all traffic through proxy + shim config until we rollback.
Maya Singh: perfect. if nobody objects, i'll open RFC stub and put a short poll in #eng-platform to decide on hybrid-first approach. :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: sounds good
Jamal Bryant: yep
Maya Singh: thanks all — closing thread, will post RFC link here shortly.
